title: Top 7 Verified Recruiting Companies in Corpus Christi, TX
excerpt: Seven recruiting agencies with a real Corpus Christi office, hand-verified for 2026 against the port and energy labor market driving local hiring.
author: Umaira Liaquat
content:
Last updated: September 2026

Search for the top recruiting companies in Corpus Christi and the results skew national fast — toll-free numbers, generic "Staffing Agency in Corpus Christi" landing pages, and at least one branch address that turns out to sit in a different city across the bay. Fifteen candidates were checked against one question: does this agency have a real, staffed office inside Corpus Christi that an employer could actually visit? Seven do.

Two are locally owned or headquartered here; five are branches of regional or national firms, disclosed as such below — including one whose own website currently displays a stale suite number for its own office, caught mid-research for this piece.

Why Corpus Christi's Recruiting Market Is Different

Corpus Christi isn't hiring like a typical mid-size Texas city, because its economy isn't built like one. The Port of Corpus Christi is the largest port in the United States by tonnage and the country's number-one gateway for crude oil exports, moving more than 200 million tons of cargo in 2023 — the second straight year it has out-tonned the Port of Houston. More than $65 billion in capital investment has gone into the port and the petrochemical and industrial ecosystem around it, crude oil exports now exceed 1.8 million barrels a day, and the ship channel has been deepened to 54 feet specifically to handle larger tankers, according to the Texas Economic Development Corporation's regional profile.

That scale creates a genuinely different labor problem than a general light-industrial market. The maritime trades workforce feeding the port skews old — industry coverage puts the median age of local maritime tradespeople at 54 — and Del Mar College's Maritime Training Center graduates only around 45 marine electricians and 30 engine-department ratings a year against a regional demand estimated at 120 to 150 annually. Layer on the LNG buildout: Trains 8 through 10 are projected to need more than 400 permanent operations and maintenance personnel through 2027, and the American Petroleum Institute's 2024 Workforce Trends Report estimates that 22% of the Gulf Coast's petrochemical technical workforce will hit retirement eligibility by 2026. An agency that's good at filling warehouse shifts isn't automatically equipped to source credentialed marine electricians or LNG operations staff against that kind of deadline.

The numbers behind the metro itself back up the scale: the Corpus Christi MSA (Nueces, San Patricio, and Aransas counties) had an estimated 2025 population of roughly 451,191, with the city proper at about 317,247, and a civilian labor force of approximately 213,700 as of April 2025 — up 6,200 year-over-year. That's a market growing fast enough, and specialized enough, that the difference between a national landing page and a real local office actually matters.

1. L.K. Jordan & Associates

L.K. Jordan & Associates was founded in Corpus Christi in 1990 by Linda K. Jordan and has run from 400 Mann Street, Suite 410, for 36 years. It's a women- and family-owned firm covering executive search, accounting and finance, administrative, healthcare, oil and gas, and skilled-trades placements — a genuinely broad spread that lines up with the mix of energy-sector and professional employers based downtown.

The firm has since expanded into Houston, Austin, and San Antonio, so it's no longer a single-location shop, but Corpus Christi is where it started and where its Texas headquarters still sits. That's worth being direct about: you're calling a regional firm's home office, not a satellite branch of an out-of-state parent.

Best fit for: an employer that wants executive-level or specialized professional search from a firm with deep, multi-decade roots in the local energy and business community.

Pricing: not published; expect a markup on the hourly bill rate for staffing placements and a percentage placement fee for direct hire and executive search.

2. All Temps Personnel Services

All Temps Personnel Services, operating as Employee Risk Management Co., LLC, has run from 321 Texan Trail, Suite 100, since it was founded on September 15, 1994 — 31 years in Corpus Christi. It's been BBB-accredited since October 2025 and holds both SBA Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Economically Disadvantaged WOSB (EDWOSB) certifications, plus a PEO license (#266), which matters for any client considering its payroll and co-employment services alongside straight staffing.

Its focus runs across light industrial, healthcare, hospitality, transportation, and janitorial placements, plus general administrative support — a wide net that overlaps with L.K. Jordan's coverage at the industrial and admin end but skews more toward hourly, high-volume roles than executive search.

Best fit for: an employer that wants a certified woman-owned local vendor for light-industrial or hospitality staffing, with the option to bundle in PEO-style payroll.

Pricing: not published; markup on the hourly bill rate for staffing, with PEO services typically priced as a percentage of payroll.

3. Labor Finders

Labor Finders' Corpus Christi branch operates from 4701 Ayers Street, Suite 205. The screenshot above shows the parent company's national homepage rather than a Corpus Christi-specific page, since the local office runs on the shared laborfinders.com franchise site; state business filings list the local operator as "L.C. Personnel DBA Labor Finders," which is disclosed here so a caller isn't surprised by the entity name on a contract. The franchise brand itself dates to 1975, giving it "over 40 years" of national history behind a locally run office.

Its specialty is squarely construction, hospitality, light industrial, manufacturing, and waste management, with named skilled trades — welding, electrical, plumbing — that overlap directly with the kind of craft labor the port and refining sector draws on.

Best fit for: an employer needing same-day or short-notice construction and light-industrial labor from a franchise with decades of national infrastructure behind a local office.

Pricing: not published; bill-rate markup for day labor and temp placements, standard across the Labor Finders franchise system.

4. Unique Employment Services

Unique Employment Services runs from 4646 Corona Drive, Suite 100. Its BBB listing shows 47 years in business, which would place its founding in the late 1970s; that figure is self-reported by the company rather than independently dated through a separate filing, so it's presented here as a self-reported figure rather than a confirmed one. Its BBB profile currently shows no letter rating due to insufficient information on file — worth noting neutrally, since an unrated profile isn't the same thing as a bad one, just a thinner public record.

The firm covers professional and clerical placements, industrial staffing, executive recruitment, and payroll services, positioning it as a generalist alongside All Temps rather than a specialist in any one vertical.

Best fit for: a Corpus Christi employer that wants a long-running local generalist covering clerical through executive-level recruitment under one roof.

Pricing: not published; bill-rate markup for staffing, placement fee for executive recruitment.

5. Remedy Intelligent Staffing

Remedy Intelligent Staffing's Corpus Christi office sits at 4444 Corona Drive, Suite 230 — one block from Unique Employment Services on the same corridor. Remedy is the franchise division of EmployBridge, which has franchised since 1988 and is, by its own description, North America's largest light-industrial staffing supplier with more than 600 locations. That scale is the point of calling a Remedy office: national sourcing infrastructure and applicant-tracking technology behind a local desk, disclosed here as a franchise branch rather than an independent local firm.

Its placements run across finance and accounting, industrial roles, and office, retail, and hospitality staffing — a similar spread to All Temps and Unique, with EmployBridge's national scale as the differentiator.

Best fit for: an employer that wants a large national staffing network's technology and sourcing reach behind a local Corpus Christi desk.

Pricing: not published; bill-rate markup for temp and temp-to-hire, standard across EmployBridge's franchise brands.

6. AtWork

AtWork's Corpus Christi franchise opened in October 2022 under local market manager Karen Barnes, named in the office's own grand-opening press release that year. Cross-checking AtWork's corporate "Places" archive, a Kompass business listing, and that press release all point to 5866 S. Staples St., Suite 402 as the correct address — but the location page itself, screenshotted above, currently displays 4466 S Staples St, a stale suite reference caught live during research for this piece. The parent AtWork brand has operated for more than 30 years; this specific office is a newer local branch of that established franchise system.

Its focus covers administrative and clerical roles, manufacturing, professional placements, warehouse staffing, hospitality, and IT — one of the broader mixes on this list, reflecting AtWork's general-staffing franchise model.

Best fit for: an employer that wants a newer, actively growing local franchise office with a broad staffing mix, provided you confirm the current suite number directly before visiting.

Pricing: not published; bill-rate markup for temp and temp-to-hire, standard across the AtWork franchise system.

7. Snelling

Snelling's Corpus Christi office lists an address of 4455 S. Padre Island Drive, Suite 121, and describes itself on its own site as "a proud locally owned and operated Snelling franchise" serving the Coastal Bend with manufacturing, logistics, warehousing, and administrative staffing.

This entry carries a genuine, stated verification gap: only one source — the company's own site — could be confirmed for this address. No independent BBB, Yelp, Google Maps, or LinkedIn listing corroborated it during this research, and the individual franchise owner's name isn't disclosed anywhere found. That doesn't mean the business isn't real; a franchise this size can absolutely be legitimate without a fully built-out public review footprint. It does mean this entry is included on weaker verification footing than the other six, and that gap is stated here rather than smoothed over.

Best fit for: an employer willing to verify the office directly by phone or visit before relying on it, given the thinner independent confirmation available for this specific listing.

Pricing: not published; bill-rate markup for temp and temp-to-hire, standard across the Snelling franchise system.

How This List Was Verified

Every firm had to clear the same three checks used throughout this series: a real, staffed office inside Corpus Christi that an employer could visit, not a service-area page; independent confirmation of that address through at least two sources where possible (Google Business Profile, the Better Business Bureau, corporate location pages, business filings, or press coverage); and a working website whose content matched the location claim. Ownership was then recorded honestly — locally owned, or a franchise branch with its parent named — because a real branch is genuinely useful to a Corpus Christi employer and a landing page is not. Fifteen candidates were reviewed in total; seven cleared the bar, one of them (Snelling) with an explicitly stated verification gap rather than being excluded outright.

Insight Global was excluded for having no physical Corpus Christi address anywhere — only a toll-free number and a generic service-area page, with its actual headquarters in Atlanta, Georgia. NES Fircroft was excluded on the same pattern: only a zip code surfaces for its "Corpus Christi" presence, no street address, behind a global staffing multinational's thin "we cover this region" page. Firman Solutions was excluded because its listed corporate headquarters — 355 Vista Glen Dr, Apt 3206, Plano, TX — reads as a residential apartment address rather than a real corporate presence, and no Corpus Christi street address could be found anywhere for it.

LEAD Staffing was excluded for a more specific reason: its "Corpus Christi" branch is actually located at 1500 Wildcat Drive, Suite F, Portland, TX 78374 — a separate city across the bay, not Corpus Christi proper — confirmed by the company's own grand-opening announcement for that location. TCW Global was excluded as a national/global brand (headquartered in San Diego) running a generic city landing-page pattern with no independently verifiable local address. Workforce Solutions Coastal Bend has a real, staffed local presence, but it's a nonprofit, publicly funded regional Workforce Development Board, not a private recruiting or staffing company, so it was left off as miscategorized rather than excluded on quality — a jobseeker or employer working with the public workforce system is doing something different from hiring a private agency.

How These 7 Agencies Compare

  • Longest continuous local roots: L.K. Jordan & Associates, founded in Corpus Christi in 1990 and still headquartered here.
  • Only combined PEO/payroll and staffing option with SBA certifications: All Temps Personnel Services, WOSB and EDWOSB certified with a PEO license.
  • Deepest craft-labor and construction network: Labor Finders, backed by a national franchise brand dating to 1975.
  • Broadest generalist mix with the longest self-reported history: Unique Employment Services, 47 years per BBB (self-reported).
  • Largest national sourcing infrastructure: Remedy Intelligent Staffing, part of EmployBridge's 600+ location network.
  • Newest actively growing local office: AtWork, opened October 2022 under local market manager Karen Barnes.
  • Weakest independent verification, included with a stated caveat: Snelling, confirmed only through its own site.

What to Check Before Signing With Any of Them

  • Confirm the current suite number before you visit — this research caught AtWork's own location page displaying a stale address for its own office
  • Ask for the markup percentage or placement fee in writing — none of these seven publish rates, and quotes vary by role and credential
  • For port, refinery, or LNG-adjacent work, ask about TWIC, OSHA 30, and site-specific safety credentialing — a firm that can't speak to these fluently isn't set up for craft-labor placement in this market
  • Get temp-to-hire conversion terms up front — the fee to convert a temp worker to your payroll is where surprises usually live
  • Check who carries workers' comp and payroll responsibility — with a PEO-style firm like All Temps this can be shared under co-employment; with a straight staffing firm it stays with the agency
  • Verify a franchise's local ownership and the entity name on your contract — Labor Finders' Corpus Christi filings list a different named operator ("L.C. Personnel DBA Labor Finders") than the national brand you'll search for

The Bottom Line

Corpus Christi's recruiting market runs on the same industrial and maritime engine that makes the port itself the busiest in the country by tonnage, and that shows in who's actually built to serve it. L.K. Jordan and All Temps are the purely local options, one skewing executive search and the other light industrial with PEO services attached. Labor Finders brings deep national craft-labor infrastructure to a local office; Unique Employment Services is the long-running local generalist; Remedy brings EmployBridge's national scale; AtWork is the newest, actively growing franchise; and Snelling rounds out the list with a caveat worth reading before you call. Five of the seven are franchise branches, and that's fine — what matters is a real, staffed office and an honest answer about who actually owns it.

Whichever you choose, the diligence is the same: confirm the current address and suite number directly, get the markup in writing, and for port, refinery, or LNG-adjacent work, ask for the safety certifications by name before a project starts, not during one.
